case_intro: Module-based automation helped a two-person QA team complete regression across more than 120 application pages while continuing to test sprint work.
case_context: A mobile device management application supported regular and promotional pricing, bundles and bonuses across providers and branches. Regression required manual checks across more than 120 pages, including browser DevTools, API requests/responses and database validation.
case_problem: The ten-day regression ran alongside the sprint, affecting production release schedules and leaving less time for QA tasks, test case preparation and user story validation documents.
case_role: Within a team of two QA professionals, I took on most of the framework design and implementation using Playwright and TypeScript, including classes, interfaces, page objects and test data.
case_core: Start with the application core: prepare mobile devices so they were active and enabled for price generation before running dependent scenarios.
case_structure: Separate each window into selectors, test data, page interaction logic and test specifications. Run tests by module through package.json scripts.
case_angular: Handle Angular modals and ng-select components with reusable helpers/utilities, waits for parent and option components, input-state checks and tracking of whether the selector was expanded. Use try-catch handling for interaction errors.
case_review: Check executions locally with the Playwright VS Code extension and reports. Investigate failures manually: report confirmed application defects in Azure DevOps; otherwise correct the automated test.
case_result: The complete regression cycle decreased from ten to five days while continuing to cover all application windows. This improvement was observed in successive regression cycles. Some modules that previously required hours could be executed in minutes.
case_manual: The five-day cycle combined automated execution, manual validation and failure review. Critical core behavior and new sprint functionality that had not yet been automated continued to receive manual testing.
case_lessons: I learned to structure a maintainable automation project and would strengthen my Node.js foundations earlier before starting a similar implementation.
case_note: Anonymized account based on my professional experience. The result describes the full regression cycle, not a 50% reduction in every individual test.

qa_case_title: qaTestGE: directing AI, validating the product
qa_case_intro: A QA workspace born from a fragmented workflow across Gemini Gems and ChatGPT projects. I direct the product and its implementation with AI assistance; development is ongoing.
qa_case_fact: Human direction · AI assistance · QA validation
qa_case_problem: I used separate assistants to prepare edge cases, UAT, sanity and other test categories. My goal is to bring case design, bugs, tags, manual test runs and exports together in one workspace for QA professionals. Faster AI-assisted case generation and feedback are product goals, not capabilities already delivered.
qa_case_role: I define features, architecture, bugs to resolve and the working context. AI helps turn those decisions into code. I use OpenCode and Codex, reusable skills and a prompt structure of Role, Context, Requirements and Output; I remain responsible for evaluating the implementation.
qa_case_roles: I organize assistance into architecture/orchestration, bug hunting, backend, frontend, code review, testing, UI and UX roles. These are development responsibilities assigned to AI assistants, not autonomous agents built into the product.
qa_case_context: AGENTS.md records project rules and MEMORY.md preserves working context. I use an Obsidian MCP connection and am starting a RAG/second-brain workflow while migrating my notes. This is part of my development process, not a search or RAG feature offered by qaTestGE.
qa_case_defect_title: A real correction: test cases need multiple steps
qa_case_defect: The first designer treated a test case as a single step. During a local end-to-end walkthrough, I found that this did not represent a QA test procedure. I clarified the requirement through a more precise prompt and corrected the design to support a sequence of actions and expected results.
qa_case_defect_result: The current repository models steps as an array with action and expectedResult, and documents up to 100 steps per saved case. The screenshot shows editable examples and explicit saving; it does not demonstrate AI generation.
qa_case_validation: The current implementation uses React, TypeScript and Vite with an Express API and PostgreSQL through pg, following an MVC-style separation. I use ESLint and Prettier for consistency and unit tests before accepting changes. The repository also contains API tests with Vitest/Supertest and CI checks.
qa_case_validation_flow: For manual validation, I simulate daily QA work: create a bug and check that the flow is understandable, accessible from the workspace and consistent with the intended use case. Linting and formatting help maintainability; they do not establish security by themselves.
qa_case_current: Management of bugs, multi-step test cases, evidence and tags; manual test runs; registration/login and account settings. Individual bugs and cases can be exported to PDF, Excel and Markdown, while the designer exports its editable examples to Excel/PDF. ExcelJS, jsPDF and SwaggerUI support export and API documentation workflows.
qa_case_limits: No connection to AI providers via API keys is implemented. The designer does not analyze the description or generate AI proposals, and test runs are manual records rather than an automated execution engine. Account settings do not imply a team/user administration module.
qa_case_next: My current priorities are test suites and user/project management. SonarQube and k6 performance testing are planned improvements; I do not present them as completed checks or claim a measured productivity gain yet.

sql_case_title: Reusable SQL: from scattered checks to a shared Wiki
sql_case_intro: I built and documented a reusable query catalogue so QA, developers and the Product Owner could retrieve the data needed for recurring use cases without rebuilding each query from scratch.
sql_case_link: Read the reusable SQL case study
sql_case_before: Multiple application tabs and endpoint responses had to be compared to find the required values.
sql_case_after: A shared Azure DevOps Wiki documented queries, their purpose, usage conditions and alternatives.
sql_case_context: The application had more than 120 pages and many related database tables. Data validation across maintenance screens required joins, filtering, grouping and ordering. Working in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), I needed to retrieve related values more directly instead of repeatedly comparing screens and API responses.
sql_case_map: For each maintenance screen, identify the base table and its relationships, using my knowledge of the application flow. This investigation and documentation took several weeks.
sql_case_queries: Combine JOIN and WHERE clauses with GROUP BY, HAVING and ORDER BY as required by the use case, so the result presented the values needed for validation.
sql_case_validate: Test queries locally before publishing. Split long queries into smaller parts, check each part, then add joins progressively and verify that the returned data and WHERE conditions matched the intended scenario.
sql_case_document: Publish each query in the Azure DevOps Wiki with a short explanation of why it existed, the specific cases where it applied and alternatives. Team members could access and update the documentation.
sql_case_procedures: Document stored procedures used within specific workflows so their execution context was available alongside the queries.
sql_case_result: The catalogue supported user story validation, certification testing, regression and production release activities. It reduced the need to recreate queries and made recurring data lookups more accessible to QA, developers and the Product Owner.
sql_case_measurement: This was a qualitative improvement in reuse and access to knowledge; I did not record a time-saving percentage or database performance benchmark.
sql_case_learning: Investigating table relationships, checking intermediate results and documenting query intent turned individual troubleshooting into a shared team resource. Reuse was supported by understanding when a query applied, rather than treating every query as interchangeable.
sql_case_note: The Wiki and queries are internal. This anonymized account describes the method and observed benefits without publishing table names, records or execution instructions.

flow_title: FlowSaldo: turning financial activity into clarity
flow_intro: A financial workspace that connects product design, backend architecture and QA. I define the requirements, guide AI-assisted development and validate complete user journeys.
flow_ready: Manage transactions, review synthetic email imports before confirming them, filter by month and currency, and understand spending through categories, budgets and cash-flow views. Account settings include currency and balance visibility preferences; login and registration currently demonstrate the visual experience.
flow_engine_title: A foundation built for reliable data
flow_engine: The API and worker separate ingestion from accounting. Idempotency prevents duplicate imports, while transactional confirmation creates a movement only once. Domain rules remain separate from the interface, and CSV export uses explicit columns and validation.
flow_ai: Provider-neutral instructions coordinate architecture, implementation, QA and review. Dedicated language and export guardian profiles support consistent copy and deliverables; the project also includes automated checks for pluralization patterns and tabular exports.
flow_next: Connect Gmail and Outlook through OAuth, expand bank-specific parsing, enable real user accounts and introduce assisted classification. These milestones extend the current review-first workflow and remain planned capabilities.
